update_color_history(track_id, color_data, frame_number)[source]

Update color history with exponential moving average.

This method keeps track of the last N frames of color data for each track ID and calculates the exponential moving average to smooth out noise in color detection. It also resets the history if the track was missing for too long.

Parameters:

  • track_id (int) – The ID of the tracked object

  • color_data (dict) – Dictionary of color percentages from current frame

  • frame_number (int) – Current frame number

Returns:

Averaged color percentages

Return type:

dict

project.detectors.byte_track_tracker module

class project.detectors.byte_track_tracker.ByteTrackTracker(output_dir, min_frames_for_averaging=2, frame_width=640, frame_height=360)[source]

Bases: BaseTracker

This class inherits from the BaseTracker class and implements the ByteTrack algorithm for multi-object tracking. It uses the Supervision library’s This class is designed to work with YOLO detection results and provides functionality for tracking objects across frames.

ByteTrack paper: Zhang, Yifu, et al. “ByteTrack: Multi-Object Tracking by Associating Every Detection Box.” ECCV 2022. https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.06864

Supervision implementation: https://github.com/roboflow/supervision

calculate_color_presence(hsv, mask)[source]

Calculate the presence of different colors in the masked HSV image. Works in two passes: first detects all colors except gray, then checks for gray presence in unclassified pixels if no other colors are dominant.

  • hsv (np.ndarray) – The HSV image.

  • mask (np.ndarray) – The mask of the region of interest.

project.detectors.yolo_detector module

class project.detectors.yolo_detector.YOLODetector(model_path='yolo11n.pt', device='auto', use_segmentation=False, skip_color_analysis=False)[source]

Bases: object

Module to perform object detection using YOLOv11 model from Ultralytics. This class is designed to detect objects in a given frame and return the detection results. The model’s weights are loaded from a specified file path.

Original YOLO architecture by Joseph Redmon et al. Model: yolov11n.pt (YOLOv11) Citation: Jocher, G., et al. (2023). Ultralytics YOLOv11. https://docs.ultralytics.com/models/yolo11/ Repository: https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics

detect_objects(frame, timestamp)[source]

Detect objects in the given frame using the YOLO model.

Parameters:

  • frame (np.ndarray) – The input image in BGR format

  • timestamp (float) – The timestamp of the frame

Returns:

A list of dictionaries containing detection results

Return type:

List[Dict[str, Any]]

Note

The function will only detect people and vehicles. This can be easily hanged by modifying the OBJECTS list in constants/constants.py.

The function will also use segmentation if the use_segmentation flag is set to True. The segmentation will be used only for the color calculation of the detected objects and not the whole frame – this is done to speed up the process as otherwise the segmentation masks would be calculated for all objects in the frame and not just the detected ones.
